text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall(s): Elevated 5xx rates and gateway timeouts for inference-gateway in us-east-1. Error spike started ~2418001200. Avg 5xx 42% across edge nodes. Sample: 429 -> 502 cascade.

Dmitri Petrov: I’m on it. grabbing logs from gateways and rate-limit service.

alice.chen: saw a flood of 429s from quota-service around the same time. tenants hitting per-tenant token limits quickly. could be a misapplied config or rollout.

ben.ortiz: copying logs: ``[gateway] upstream_error tenant=acme-corp status=502 upstream=runtime-03 token_cost=12000`` and ``[quota] quota_check tenant=acme-corp result=DENY reason=burst_limit_exceeded``. lots of high token-cost streaming requests.

carol.ng: Customer support: several customers reporting degraded responses and timeouts. major customers in us-east-1 (acme, finco). Escalating to AMs.

Dmitri Petrov: Quick impact summary for pager — 30min window: 15% of requests return 5xx, several enterprise tenants report timeouts, autoscale didn't help due to quota denies upstream.

eva.lopez: Can we throttle by tenant or apply emergency global fallback to model-variant that is cheaper? Avoid full 5xx waterfall.

alice.chen: hypothesis: quota service rollout 2418001195 pushed new burst policy with aggressive per-tenant short-window caps. It looks like a bad default for long-running streaming calls.

ben.ortiz: I’ll confirm config. hitting policy service: ``curl -s -X GET https://policy.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme-corp | jq .burst`` returns ``{"window_ms":2000,"limit":5}`` — that will kill long streams.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2417999000 (policy-service) was rolled out to prod at 2418001194 by ci-cd.

Dmitri Petrov: ok rollback candidate. Two possible mitigations: 1) rollback policy-service to previous stable, 2) hotpatch global default quotas to restore higher burst for streaming endpoints. Which is faster?

alice.chen: Hotpatching quotas is faster. we can update global policy to exclude streaming paths. doing a test patch now in staging then prod.

ben.ortiz: Patch command: ``kubectl -n infra exec -it policy-service-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/config -d "{\"path_exceptions\": [\"/v1/stream\"] , \"default_burst\": 100 }'``

alice.chen: applied to prod (rolled to 3/3 policy replicas) at 2418001256. Observability: quota deny rate dropped sharply.

Dmitri Petrov: Gateway 5xx rate dropping from 42% -> 8% in 90s. latency improving. :white_check_mark:

carol.ng: I’m telling impacted customers we saw a misconfiguration in quota rollout causing transient rate limits. ETA for full recovery?

alice.chen: Still seeing residual failures for long-lived streams that hit upstream connection resets. I’m instructing runtime teams to enable `graceful-fallback` for streaming endpoints: route requests to degraded-variant that uses smaller context/kernels.

ben.ortiz: Patch to runtime routing: ``POST /admin/route-fallbacks {"selector":"streaming","variant":"low_cost_v1","ttl":600}`` executed at 2418001278. Throughput restored for most tenants.

support-bot: Noted: create incident ticket INC-241800 for follow-up, notify AMs, add affected tenant list.

Dmitri Petrov: Handoff: I’ll stay for 30 minutes to ensure stability, then hand to morning oncall @eva.lopez. Next steps before handoff: confirm deploy rollback vs improved config, run canary for policy-service, and draft customer communication.

eva.lopez: I’ll take next shift. please add a timeline and list of exact mitigations to the incident ticket.

alice.chen: short timeline added to INC-241800: 2418001194 policy rollout -> 2418001200 429 spike -> 2418001256 quota hotpatch -> 2418001278 runtime fallback -> 2418001296 5xx<5%.

carol.ng: Sending initial customer note: "We identified a quota configuration change that caused cascading rate limits and timeouts. We applied emergency fixes to quota service and routing to restore service. Our teams are working on root cause and remediation. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

ben.ortiz: root cause looks like a missing exception for streaming endpoints in the new policy schema + overly aggressive default burst. Change landed in policy-service PR #912 but the schema change lacked test for long-lived connections.

Dmitri Petrov: Postmortem TODOs: - revert policy-service PR or add explicit streaming exception (owner: ben.ortiz) - add unit/integration test for streaming quota behavior (owner: alice.chen) - improve canary rollout checks for policy changes (owner: deploy-team) - customer follow-up template and list (owner: carol.ng).

deploy-bot: Scheduled rollback job for policy-service created: rollback-241800-window (will not execute automatically until manual confirm).

alice.chen: creating replay of the 429->502 chain to reproduce in staging. will attach logs to INC-241800.

eva.lopez: Thanks team. Good mitigation. I’ll take over monitoring and coordinate postmortem tomorrow 10:30am PT. Marking this thread for handoff.

Dmitri Petrov: leaving handoff notes in ticket and Slack. setting severity to Sev2 -> monitoring for 2 hours.

incident-bot: Incident updated: Sev2 -> monitoring. Acknowledged by eva.lopez.

carol.ng: closing customer comms loop for initial notice. will follow with detailed RCA after postmortem.

alice.chen: logging complete. final metrics show error rate back to baseline.

Dmitri Petrov: signing off from pager. good job everyone. :raised_hands:
